name: Worthing

licensing.selective: No selective licensing scheme found in force. In March 2024 the council agreed to consult on and scope a selective licensing scheme for Heene, Central and Selden wards; no designation had been confirmed when checked.
licensing.additional: No additional HMO licensing scheme; only national mandatory HMO licensing applies (five or more people from two or more households).

housing: Worthing is a seaside town where private renting is above the South East average, much of it in Regency, Victorian and Edwardian houses split into flats in the town centre, Heene and Central wards. Modern apartment blocks line parts of the seafront. Further out, Goring, Durrington and Findon Valley are mainly interwar and post-war bungalows and semis, with many older owner-occupiers. The council has looked at selective licensing for the central wards where private lets are concentrated.
checkinTips: Victorian and Regency houses split into flats in the centre and Heene: photograph communal halls, fire doors and meters, and count keys and fobs.
Seafront flats: photograph window frames, balconies and metal fittings for salt and wind damage, and note any condensation or mould.
Basement and ground-floor flats in converted houses: check for damp, ventilation and the condition of lightwells.
Bungalows in Goring and Findon Valley: photograph gardens, garages, conservatories and any mobility adaptations.
Flats over shops on Montague Street and Chapel Road: note separate entrances, rear access and bin storage.
Homes on the shingle coast: check airbricks and gardens for flood or storm damage.
tenantHelp: Adur & Worthing Councils' private sector housing team investigates disrepair, damp and unsafe conditions in private rented homes and licenses HMOs.
